title: Terms
text: Time 10 min Difficulty Easy Steps 10 terms You will need Nothing, just read entropy The randomness from the dice, the raw material the 24 words are built from. airgap Tails booted with networking Disabled . The computer forgets the session on shutdown. 2-of-3 Any two of three keys can spend. One alone cannot. m/48'/0'/0'/2' The wallet’s path. Confirmed on screen , never typed from memory. Not a secret. PSBT The unsigned payment file, carried on the USB. The seed never leaves the offline computer. descriptor / xpub The wallet map / a watch key. Both watch , neither spends . BIP39 The 2,048-word list the 24 words come from. hash · fingerprint The file’s fingerprint must match the project’s published one, every character . signature The project confirming the file. “Good signature” , or the file is deleted. zero-trust Nobody’s word is taken. Two tools must agree.

title: Before you begin
text: Time 15 min Difficulty Easy Steps 1 worksheet You will need Pen and paper Don't trust, verify. The seed phrase is the wallet. The device only signs. Anyone who holds the words holds the coins. No device can stop them. Check every threat you actually care about. The guide answers each one under its checkbox. ONE SEED, STOLEN OR LOST Buys an attacker nothing → THE VAULT NEEDS TWO TWO PLATES + THE MAP Rebuilds the wallet → FROM ANY TWO PLACES What am I protecting against? ☐ Theft: burglar, coercion, the $5 wrench One stolen seed buys an attacker nothing. They need a second, in another place. ☐ Fire, flood, disaster: one location stops existing Three places, stamped titanium. Two surviving plates plus the map rebuild the wallet. ☐ My own mistakes: lost paper, copied a word wrong Two tools must agree on every word before anything is stamped. ☐ Scams: an email or a site that looks official asks for my words Words into the device itself, during recovery, nowhere else. No hardware company will ever ask for your seed phrase. A message that asks is the attack. ☐ Death or incapacitation: heirs who aren't Bitcoiners The inheritance sheet, written for a non-Bitcoiner, kept where your family can find it. Note Read it back: checked theft and disaster, the 2-of-3 is built for you. Checked scams, or coins somewhere with a seed you do not fully control, the single-sig sheet is your door. Where are your coins right now? ☐ On an exchange. The exchange holds the keys, so the exchange holds the coins. ☐ In a phone app or software wallet. Your words have lived on a connected device. Treat that seed as exposed. This makes a fresh seed the offline way and moves the coins onto it. Your old device can stay on as the signer. ☐ On a hardware wallet, one seed. You are closer than you think. This is your upgrade path: check how the seed was born, add a passphrase, stamp the words in metal, set up a watch-only wallet. ☐ Nowhere yet. Start at the beginning. Work the steps. Next, the checklist. Pick your path The doors above state where you stand today. After the doors, pick the trade that fits. The switch below routes you to the right starting sheet. title: Checklist
text: Time 30 min + shopping Difficulty Moderate Steps 11 items You will need This sheet · A budget for the kit Gather everything on this list before the first boot, so nothing has to be ordered in the middle of the build. On the table The dice table Five casino dice with readable faces Pencil and the recording grid A private room , no camera 1 The computer One machine, two boots Boot 1: stays online, watch-only, never holds a seed Boot 2: Tails USB, networking off Data USB: carries only checked files ✓ Files Checked before anything goes offline Tails 7.13 · Sparrow 2.5.5 (exact) · Electrum 4.8.2 Ian Coleman page (offline only) · dice converter (in this kit) Metal Three plates, three places Three titanium plates , one seed on each StampSeed kit holds 1 (buy 2 more) · Cryptotag holds 2 (buy 1 more). Don’t mix methods Three places, far enough apart that one disaster can’t take all three Nothing is bought mid-build. If a plate or USB is missing when its sheet arrives, stop and get it first.

title: Check the files
text: Time 30 min Difficulty Careful Steps 7 sections You will need The downloaded files · Two verification tools Every file gets checked before the computer goes offline, and a file that fails is deleted, no exceptions. A compromised file compromises the funds. Warning Is this the real site? These instructions only protect you on plebumbtc.io . Before you trust them: check the address bar. The domain must read exactly plebumbtc.io , no extra words, no lookalikes. Click the lock icon and confirm the certificate belongs to plebumbtc.io. Anyone can copy these pages; only the real domain gets the real updates. If anything looks wrong, stop. Verify through a second channel before continuing. What is required The downloads from the checklist: Tails 7.13, Sparrow 2.5.5, Electrum 4.8.2, the Ian Coleman page, and the dice converter from this kit. Step 1 · Download only from the real sites. Tails tails.net ✓ Sparrow github.com ✓ Electrum electrum.org ✓ Ian Coleman github.com ✓ NOT A LOOK-ALIKE PAGE · NOT FROM THIS SITE (EXCEPT THE DICE CONVERTER) Sparrow must be 2.5.5 exactly. A newer download will not match. That is a stop, not an upgrade. The dice converter is the one file this site provides; its fingerprint is in VERIFY.md. Step 2 · Compare the fingerprint. Every character. FILE ⭳ a3f9…c41d your computer computes this compare with the fingerprint on the project's own site EVERY CHARACTER MATCHES ✓ · ONE DIFFERS = DELETE Windows: PowerShell → Get-FileHash. Mac: Terminal → shasum -a 256. Paste the result next to the fingerprint published on the project's own site. Step 3 · Check the signature. Want: "Good signature". $ gpg --verify sparrow-2.5.5-manifest.txt.asc gpg: Good signature gpg: WARNING: This key is not certified with a trusted signature! ↑ that warning is normal. The fingerprint match is what matters Import the signing key, confirm its fingerprint, then verify. The "not certified" warning is normal on first import. What matters: the line says Good signature and the fingerprint matches. Sparrow signing key fingerprint: D4D0D3202FC06849A257B38DE94618334C674B40. Electrum (ThomasV): 6694D8DE7BE8EE5631BED9502BD5824B7F9470E6. Step 4 · Run the kit check. $ ./verify_kit.sh tails-amd64-7.13.img … PASS sparrowwallet-2.5.5 … PASS dice-converter … PASS Put the downloads next to verify_kit.sh and run it. It checks the pinned fingerprints. One failure: the work stops. Later · Two tools must agree. Every time. DICE CONVERTER abandon ability … … art IAN COLEMAN (OFFLINE) abandon ability … … art = SAME BITS → SAME WORDS · SAME SEED → SAME ADDRESSES · SAME PAYMENT DETAILS Same dice bits → same 24 words in both tools. Same seed → same first addresses in Sparrow and Electrum. The wallet map shows those same addresses. Before signing, both tools show the same destination, amount, change, and fee. If they differ, stop. Stop if A fingerprint differs by one character: delete the file. The signature isn't Good: delete the file. The two tools disagree: stop. Next, Two boots.

title: Two boots
text: Time 45 min Difficulty Careful Steps 4 sections You will need Everyday computer · Tails USB Boot 1 · Network on This computer Watches balances. Builds a payment. Never holds a seed. Network on Verify files Watch-only wallet Export unsigned file then shut down Boot 2 · Networking off Tails USB This stick is the offline computer. It borrows the hardware, then forgets. Networking off One seed in memory Sign the file Full shutdown after One computer, used twice. The first boot watches the wallet and broadcasts finished payments. It never holds a seed. The second boot is the Tails USB: networking off, exactly one seed, then a full shutdown. The seed lives in memory only. Shutdown wipes it. BOOT 1 · ONLINE 👁 WATCH · NEVER A SEED BOOT 2 · TAILS 1 SEED NETWORK OFF · THEN ⏻ ⇄ SAME COMPUTER · SHUT DOWN FULLY BETWEEN What "airgapped" means here Yes: Networking Disabled on the Tails welcome screen, before the desktop. Files cross on the data USB: payment files, the map, checked programs. The online computer stays watch-only. Not airgapped: Turning networking off after Sparrow opened. Unplugging a disk that was online yesterday. A photo of a seed. A password manager, printer, or cloud note as backup. Prepare the two USBs TAILS USB checked file → written with official installer DATA USB only checked files labeled DATA NO PERSISTENT STORAGE. THE DRIVE STAYS AMNESIC Download Tails only from the official site. Check the signature and checksum before writing. Write it with the official installer, label it TAILS. Do not create Persistent Storage. Skip the passphrase. The data USB gets only files that already passed the checks. Every offline session Boot the Tails drive. Networking Disabled. Don't unlock Persistent Storage. Copy only the file that session needs from the data USB. Do the work: convert dice, restore one seed, sign one file, or export the map. Copy the result back to the data USB. Shut down fully. Dark screen before the drive comes out. Stop if Two seeds in one session: never. Networking turns on while a seed is in memory: that session is burned. Tails offers Persistent Storage: don't create it, don't unlock it. Stronger (optional): a dedicated old laptop with the Wi-Fi card physically pulled. Ethernet never plugged. The Tails file is still checked, networking still Disabled, data USB still clean. The stick remains the only wire. Next, Make the three keys.

title: Make the three keys
text: Time 30-45 min Difficulty Moderate Steps 4 sections You will need 5 dice · Paper and pen · The worksheet SHAKE 1 SHAKE 2 SHAKE 3 11 RE-ROLL 01 00 10 01 01 RE-ROLL 11 11 00 10 00 10 RE-ROLL 00 01 RE-ROLL 10 256-BIT STRING 11 00 10 01 01 01 11 00 10 11 00 10 00 01 10 …keep rolling… 256 / 256 BITS 10 / 256 20 / 256 30 / 256 256 / 256 24 WORDS Roll as many times as needed to get 256 bits of entropy: about 39 shakes. Warning Never enter seed words on an online computer. This work starts after Tails has booted with networking set to Disabled, and before any plate is stamped. Five casino dice are required, and every face has to be readable. Faces 1 through 4 are kept. Faces 5 and 6 are rolled again. The work is done three times, for three keys, and the computer is shut down fully between them. A private room, no camera. The faces 1 is 00. 2 is 01. 3 is 10. 4 is 11. 5 and 6 are not bits. Roll those dice again. Read the dice left to right, the same way every shake. Example: 4, 6, 1, 3, 2 becomes 11, skip the 6, then 00, 10, 01. Write only 0 and 1. Roll exactly 256 bits (128 pairs, about 39 shakes), then stop. More bits do not add security (everything folds down to 256), and extra bits make the two tools below disagree, which stops the work for no reason. Turn the bits into 24 words 01 · Boot Tails. Networking Disabled. Copy the checked converter and the Ian Coleman page from the data USB to the Desktop. 02 · Run the converter. Paste the bits. It prints 24 words. Word 24 is the check. Do not invent it. Do not “fix” it. 03 · Open the Ian Coleman page in the offline browser. Entropy type: Binary. 24 words. Paste the same bits. The 24 words must match. If they differ, stop. Do not pick the prettier list. 04 · Write the 24 words on the grid. Read them back out loud once. 05 · Shut Tails down. Wait until the screen is dark. Then start the next key. Seed 2 is a new set of rolls. Seed 3 is a new set of rolls. Never continue a list from the previous boot. $ cd ~/Desktop$ python3 bip39_dice_converter.py The last word is a check The 24 words are not 24 free choices. The last word carries a short check so a copying mistake is caught before metal is stamped. At least two of these checks are used. If they disagree, the work stops. Two tools, same bits, same 24 words. Converter, then the offline Ian Coleman page. Do not pick the prettier list. Let the wallet refuse a bad list. Sparrow or Electrum, networking off, will open a valid list and reject a broken one. If it will not open, do not change a word to force it. The math, if it needs to be seen. Twenty-four words are 264 bits. The first 256 are the dice. The last 8 are the check. Only word 24 can change to make that true. It is not chosen. The converter appends it after the file has been checked. Practice grid Use the printed recording grid in the bench sheet PDF. Each seed needs about 39 shakes for 256 bits. Count the pairs as you go and stop at 128. Next, Build the 2-of-3. What happens next Once the words are made, the path forks. Pick what happens next. Easy One key Full program ← Less work, more trust More work, less trust → Why about 39 shakes: the How many dice rolls page lists the old counts and the corrected math. title: Build the 2-of-3
text: Time 45-60 min Difficulty Careful Steps 9 sections You will need The three paper keys · Verified Sparrow Warning Never enter seed words on an online computer. Three public keys go into Sparrow, and no seed ever touches this build. What comes out is the wallet map, which can watch the money and never spend it. You will boot Tails four times: once per seed to copy its public key, then once more with no seed to build the vault. What is required The data USB with the checked Sparrow file (sparrowwallet-2.5.5-x86_64.tar.gz) The three paper seeds. Only one comes out per boot. Step 1 · Boot Tails. Networking stays off. NETWORKING DISABLED ✓ IF THE NETWORK IS ON: STOP The entire sheet happens with networking Disabled. Check it on every boot. Step 2 · Open the terminal. Launch Sparrow. $ cd ~/Desktop $ tar -xvf sparrowwallet-2.5.5-x86_64.tar.gz $ cd Sparrow $ ./bin/Sparrow ▊ Type these four lines, one at a time. Wait for the prompt to come back after each. $ cd ~/Desktop $ tar -xvf sparrowwallet-2.5.5-x86_64.tar.gz $ cd Sparrow $ ./bin/Sparrow Wait 15 to 30 seconds. Sparrow opens. Type exactly. Spaces count. If a line turns red, stop. Step 3 · New wallet: 2 of 3, native Segwit. 1 2 3 4 Policy Type: Multi Signature HD. Script Type: Native Segwit (P2WSH). M of N: 2 / 3. The slider sits on 2, with 3 cosigners in total. Number 3 sits in the white space to the left of Cosigners and M of N. Keystore tabs: 1, 2 and 3. Each one gets filled in turn. Real Sparrow screenshot, dummy keys only. No xpub is shown in this shot. File → New Wallet. Pick Multi Signature, Native Segwit, 2 of 3. The path must read m/48'/0'/0'/2'. Anything else: stop. Step 4 · Keystore 1: Seed 1 in, public key out. SEED 1 24 words SPARROW s1-xpub.txt xpub6C...9f2k → data USB THEN: CLOSE · SHUT DOWN · DARK SCREEN Keystore 1 → New or Imported Software Wallet → type Seed 1's 24 words. Export the xpub. Save it to the data USB as s1-xpub.txt. Close Sparrow. Shut down. Wait for a dark screen. Step 5 · Twice more. One seed per boot. SEED 2 → s2-xpub.txt ⏻ SEED 3 → s3-xpub.txt ⏻ NEVER CONTINUE FROM THE PREVIOUS BOOT Boot again for Seed 2 → s2-xpub.txt. Shut down. Boot again for Seed 3 → s3-xpub.txt. Shut down. Step 6 · Fresh boot. No seed. Build the vault. 1 2 3 Master fingerprint: check it against the key it came from. Derivation: m/48'/0'/0'/2'. Anything else, stop. xpub field: this is where s1-xpub.txt goes. The value is blacked out here because it is a dummy key, and a reader must never copy a screenshot key. 1 2 3 Keystore 3, filled the same way as Keystore 1 and Keystore 2. Descriptor: wsh(sortedmulti(2, Keystore1, Keystore2, Keystore3)). That file is the wallet map. Apply: enabled only when all three keystores are filled. Click it to build the vault. Real Sparrow screenshots, dummy keys only, xpub values blacked out. Step 4 keeps its diagram, because seed words are never photographed. Boot Tails again. Do not type any seed. New wallet → Multi Signature → Native Segwit → 2 of 3 → import the three xpub files. Confirm the path. Export the output descriptor to the data USB. That file is the wallet map. Stop Confirm the first address on a second screen. Sparrow built your wallet from your seeds. But if malware sat on the build machine, it could show you an address it controls while you trust it. A second screen the malware can't reach closes that hole. Do not fund the wallet until this matches. 1 · Build in Sparrow. Finish the 2-of-3 build on the airgapped machine as usual. Write down the first receiving address it shows. Write the full string, not the QR code. 2 · Cross-check in Electrum. Rebuild the same 2-of-3 in Electrum offline from the same seeds and compare the first address. This catches entry mistakes. 3 · NEW: Display it on a second device. Load the wallet as watch-only (xpubs / wallet descriptor only, never seeds) on your phone or a second computer. Compare the first receiving address character for character . If all three agree, the coordinator didn't lie. If anything differs, stop and rebuild. Step 7 · Watch-only on the everyday computer. 👁 WATCH ONLY THIS COMPUTER NEVER HOLDS A SEED On the everyday computer, open Sparrow and import the map as a watch-only wallet. It can see the money. It can never spend it. Stop if The path doesn't read m/48'/0'/0'/2': stop. Don't type a different path. Networking is on at any point: stop. You're tempted to type a second seed without shutting down: stop. One seed per boot. Next, Practice spend.

title: Rehearse on testnet
text: Time 30 min Difficulty Moderate Steps 2 sections You will need Sparrow · Free testnet coins Before any plate exists, do the entire flow with play money : build the 2-of-3, receive, sign with two keys, shut down between sessions, broadcast. The clicks are identical to mainnet. Mistakes here cost nothing and teach everything. Warning Testnet coins are worthless. They cannot be sold, converted, or spent as real bitcoin. That is the point: there is nothing at stake except your learning. Do not "test" with real bitcoin. The rehearsal Get testnet coins from a faucet. Make a testnet address in Sparrow (network: testnet ), paste it into a faucet, wait for confirmation. This is the only step that touches the internet with your test wallet. Fine, it's worthless. Build the 2-of-3 in Sparrow on testnet. Generate three throwaway test seeds. Roll dice if you like the ritual, but these get discarded afterward. Import them into Sparrow, build the 2-of-3, verify the first receiving address on a second screen (same as the mainnet sheet). Receive the faucet coins. Send the tBTC to your test wallet's first receiving address. Watch the transaction confirm. This is your first look at how receive works, on coins that don't matter. Two-key sign with a shutdown between. Build a small spend, sign with key 1, shut the machine down , boot fresh, sign with key 2, broadcast. This is the exact airgap shutdown ritual the mainnet practice spend demands. Rehearse it here where a forgotten step costs nothing. Broadcast and confirm. Send the test coins onward (back to the faucet if it accepts returns, or to a second test address you control). Watch it confirm on a testnet block explorer. You just completed the whole loop. Stop Rule: never reuse test seeds on mainnet. When the rehearsal is done, the test seeds are burned. They do not get stamped, written down, or kept. Graduate when You built, received, two-key-signed across a shutdown, and broadcast, without the sheet open. If any step felt shaky, repeat it on testnet. The plates come after you're bored of succeeding on testnet.

title: Practice spend
text: Time 45 min Difficulty Careful Steps 5 sections You will need Two seeds · Tails USB · A small test amount THE AIRGAP SHUTDOWN · NEW SESSION ONLINE OFFLINE CREATE TRANSACTION BROADCAST TRANSACTION SEED 1 SEED 2 1 OF 2 2 OF 2 1 Create. Watch-only builds the transaction. The file is an empty outline. 2 Seed 1 signs. The file fills halfway. 1 of 2. 3 Shutdown. The file stops at the red line: full shutdown, new session, then crosses deliberately. 4 Seed 2 signs. The file fills whole. 2 of 2. 5 Broadcast. Up and right, across the airgap. The twice-signed file goes out. Warning Never enter seed words on an online computer. The practice spend uses a small amount, enough to pay a fee and no more. Write the destination, amount, and fee on paper before anything is exported, and read those notes again before each signature. Step 1 · Build the spend (online, watch-only). 👁 WATCH ONLY SEND tx-unsigned .psbt READ EVERY FIELD AGAINST THE PAPER NOTE Open watch-only Sparrow. Send tab: destination, amount, fee. Finalize for signing. Export tx-unsigned.psbt to the data USB. Step 2 · Seed 1 signs (Tails, networking off). TAILS network off SEED 1 only tx-unsigned ✍ tx-partial-s1 ⏻ FULL SHUTDOWN Boot Tails, networking disabled. Restore Seed 1 only. Open tx-unsigned.psbt, confirm the fields against the paper, sign. Export tx-partial-s1.psbt. Full shutdown. Step 3 · Seed 2 signs (fresh boot). TAILS fresh boot SEED 2 only tx-partial-s1 ✍ tx-signed ✓✓ ⏻ FULL SHUTDOWN Fresh Tails boot. Restore Seed 2 only. Open tx-partial-s1.psbt. Confirm the first signature and that the spend is unchanged. Sign. Export tx-signed.psbt. Full shutdown. Step 4 · Broadcast (online computer). 👁 WATCH ONLY 📡 BROADCAST txid → workbook Watch-only Sparrow: open the fully signed file, confirm the fields are unchanged, broadcast. Record the txid in the recovery workbook. Keys on hardware later? Generate the seed on airgapped Tails first, then import the finished 24 words. Never let the device roll its own entropy for this stack. Two keys on two brands (Foundation Passport, Blockstream Jade, BitBox02, SeedSigner/Krux; official shops only). Never three of the same box. Stop if The fields don't match the paper note: stop. Sparrow and Electrum disagree about the file: do not sign. Test with a small amount first. Always. Next, Metal and the map.

title: Metal and the map
text: Time 1-2 hours Difficulty Moderate Steps 4 sections You will need Titanium plates · Metal stamp set · The paper keys S1 🏠 HOME SAFE S2 🏢 OFF-SITE 1 S3 🏦 OFF-SITE 2 THREE PLATES THREE PLACES A small payment has gone out and come back. Now the keys leave paper for good. Three titanium plates. One seed per plate. Three separate places. If two plates sleep in the same house, the separation is gone, and the single point of failure is back. The plates One seed per plate. Never two. StampSeed (recommended): the kit holds 1 plate, buy 2 more. Cryptotag: the kit holds 2, buy 1 more. Pick one method; don't mix them. Three places, far enough apart that one fire, flood, or burglary can't take all three. No photo, no note, no password manager, no email. Any copy outside the plates is a leak. How to stamp 01 · Private room, no camera. Plate on a solid block, each letter stamped deep. 02 · Words numbered 1 to 24. Label the plate quietly: S1. No names, no "Bitcoin." 03 · Read the plate back against the paper. A mis-stamp is a bricked backup. 04 · Restore from the plate on offline Tails. First addresses must match. 05 · Only then destroy the paper, and the bit notes with it. The home plate These 24 words, alone, open a small wallet. Leave a little bitcoin there: a thief who loads only those words may stop at what they find. The same words plus a written passphrase open a modest spending wallet. The passphrase lives on paper. Never on the plate, never in the same drawer. No passphrase on the 2-of-3 itself. The shows the full setup: passphrase on paper apart from the plate, a watch-only wallet, and a test send before real money moves. Where each plate lives Plate A: Seed 1, home safe. Never Seed 2 or 3 here. Plate B: Seed 2, off-site #1. Not the same address as A or C. Plate C: Seed 3, off-site #2. Not the same address as A or B. Print the output descriptor and keep it with Plate A, plus one copy off-site, never beside all three seeds. Hardware wallets don't replace these plates. Once a year: restore from the plates, receive dust, spend dust, update locations. Write a letter pointing to the packet and which two locations matter, not the words. Next, Hide the wallet map.

title: Hide the wallet map
text: Time 30 min Difficulty Careful Steps 7 sections You will need descriptor_obfuscator.py (verified) · A dice passphrase Geography 3 seeds, secured separately in 3 different locations HOUSE 1 Plate A Seed 1 only Home safe / fire box Wallet map lives here too (the map is not a third seed) HOUSE 2 Plate B Seed 2 only Different building, different risk A copy of the map may sit here HOUSE 3 Plate C Seed 3 only Another town or trusted party Do not park Seed 1 or 2 here Geography: three plates in three places. No single point of failure. The map can watch the money, but it cannot spend. The plates are not the map, and the map is not a seed. Anyone who can read it can see the balance, so it never sits around as plain text. What is required The wallet map on the data USB, called map.txt only while you work. descriptor_obfuscator.py from the kit. Checked before it's copied. A passphrase. Not a seed, not the decoy passphrase, never stamped on a plate. Generate the passphrase with real dice: Diceware passphrase mapper . Download the page and run it in an offline Tails session, never in an everyday browser. Tails, networking Disabled. Not the everyday computer. Step 1 · Boot Tails. Copy the tool and the map. Open the demo full screen TAILS network off DESKTOP obfuscator.py map.txt NEVER OPEN THE MAP ON A PHONE Boot Tails, networking Disabled. Copy the tool and map.txt to the Desktop. Step 2 · Run the tool. Choose E. Enter the passphrase. Open the demo full screen $ python3 descriptor_obfuscator.py [E]ncrypt / [D]ecrypt? E Paste wallet map: wsh(sortedmulti(2,…)) Passphrase: •••••••••• wrote map.txt.gpg ✓ Open the terminal. Run the tool. Choose E. Paste the wallet map. Enter the passphrase. It is not a seed. One star shows for each character you type. The words themselves never appear. Use a screen nobody else can see. $ python3 descriptor_obfuscator.py Step 3 · Copy the locked file. Delete the plain one. map.txt.gpg 🔒 locked USB 1 USB 2 map.txt 🗑 EMPTY THE TRASH Copy map.txt.gpg to two USB drives. Delete map.txt from the Desktop and the USB. Empty the trash. Step 4 · Write the passphrase on paper. Twice. PASSPHRASE place #1 PASSPHRASE place #2 AWAY FROM THE PLATES · AWAY FROM THE USBs Two copies, two separate places. This paper is a single point of failure for every encrypted copy of the map. Treat it like a plate. Step 5 · Prove it opens. Check the first address. [E]ncrypt / [D]ecrypt? D (later offline boot) Passphrase: •••••••••• first address: bc1q…7x2k ✓ MATCHES On a later offline boot, choose D. The map must open, and the first address must match what you wrote down. If a plain copy was ever made, encrypt it again, then delete the plain one. If the passphrase is lost, the coins aren't gone, as long as all three plates still exist. Three seeds rebuild the map exactly. Two seeds cannot. Write the path m/48'/0'/0'/2' on the inheritance sheet. It is not a secret. Stop if You want the xpubs on paper "just in case": that's a leak. Stop. You want to invent a homemade cipher: stop. Use the tool. The passphrase is a seed or is stamped on a plate: start over with a different one. Next, If I am gone.

title: If I am gone
text: Time 1 hour Difficulty Moderate Steps 6 sections You will need Your finished kit · Your trusted person This page is for someone who has never used Bitcoin . Read it before touching a plate. One plate cannot move the long-term fund. It needs any two plates plus the wallet map . ✟ Never type the words into a phone or a website . ✟ Never photograph the plates. ✟ Never put both plates into one device. ✟ Never buy a device from a marketplace or a link in a message. PLATE A find it + PLATE B find it + MAP decrypt it TWO PLATES + THE MAP. LEAVE THE THIRD PLATE WHERE IT IS 1 Find two plates in two places. Leave the third where it is. You only need two. 2 Find the wallet map. If it asks for a passphrase, that paper is stored away from the plates . Decrypt it on a trusted computer, or with someone who can follow the map sheet. The map is not the words. 3 Buy two signing devices. Two different makers. A Jade from Blockstream’s own shop. A BitBox from BitBox’s own shop. Not two of the same box. 4 One plate per device. Plate A into one device. Plate B into the other. Never both plates in one device. 5 Load the map on both. So both devices are looking at the same fund. The path is m/48'/0'/0'/2' . That line is not a secret. 6 Send a small test first. If the test arrives, the fund can move. If the devices disagree, stop . Don’t force it. Note The home plate is a decoy. Its words alone open a small wallet. That is not the long-term fund. The fund still needs a second plate. Don’t mistake the home balance for the whole savings. If the wallet is the spending wallet. The steps above move the long-term fund. The spending wallet works differently. It has one plate and one passphrase paper. No map. No second plate. PLATE find it + PAPER passphrase → DEVICE restore both ONE PLATE PLUS THE PAPER OPENS THE SPENDING WALLET 1 Find the plate. One plate, in its place. 2 Find the passphrase paper. It lives apart from the plate, never on it. Without it, the plate opens an empty wallet. 3 Find the owner’s note. It says which device restores this wallet. If there is no note, buy that kind of device from the maker’s own shop. Never a used device, never a marketplace device. 4 Restore the plate plus the passphrase on the device. Words go into the device only. Never a phone, never a website. 5 Send a small test first. If the test arrives, the spending wallet can move. If the address looks wrong, stop. Do not mistake the spending balance for the whole savings. The long-term fund still needs two plates and the map, from the steps above.

title: If you get stuck
text: Time 10 min Difficulty Easy Steps 7 questions You will need Nothing, find your question Find the question that matches your problem. When in doubt, stop is always a valid step. What am I actually making? Three keys, made at home with dice, on a computer with no internet. Any two can spend; one cannot. The keys are stamped into titanium and kept in three places. A hardware wallet is optional, and it never creates the keys. I already own a hardware wallet. Do I start there? No. It stays in the drawer until the plates exist and a small payment has moved. If a key later goes on a device, the second key goes on a different maker’s device. All three never go on hardware. The plates are the backup. The download is newer than the version on the sheet. Stop. This kit checks Tails 7.13, Sparrow 2.5.5, Electrum 4.8.2. A newer file will not match. That is a stop, not an upgrade. Delete it. The two word lists don’t match. Stop. Don’t pick the nicer list. Don’t “fix” word 24. Roll again or find the copying mistake. A fixed word is a destroyed key. Can I keep the words in a password manager? No. A photo, note, password manager, or email is one hacked account from the whole seed. Words go on metal. The map is encrypted; its passphrase is on paper, away from the plates. What if the map, or its passphrase, is lost? Three plates rebuild the map exactly, so the coins aren’t gone. But two plates cannot . The third key can’t be derived from the other two. Back up the passphrase paper in two places, away from the plates. (Full rule on the map sheet.) What does my family do? Hand them the “If I am gone” sheet. Two plates and the map. A Jade and a BitBox from the makers’ own shops, one plate per device. No Tails. No typing words into a phone.

title: Tough questions
text: Time 15 min Difficulty Easy Steps 6 questions You will need Nothing, read and discuss You typed the seed on a laptop. Isn’t that exposed? Typed on Tails, networking off, one seed per boot, then a full shutdown. Tails forgets the session. A hardware keylogger is still possible. But one captured seed still can’t spend : the fund needs two. Never type two seeds on one boot. Why not start with a hardware wallet? A signer can join later; it is not how these keys are made. The randomness is dice you can watch . No chip to trust, no firmware to audit. Is dice randomness weaker than a hardware RNG? No. 256 bits is 256 bits , whatever made them. If the map passphrase is lost, are the coins gone? Not with all three plates. They rebuild the map exactly. But two plates plus a lost passphrase means the addresses are unrecoverable . Back up the passphrase paper in two places, away from the plates and USBs. What if someone finds one plate? They can’t spend. One key alone opens nothing. But never keep two plates in one place : that’s the whole lock in one drawer. Shouldn’t I add a passphrase to the multisig? No. The security is the distribution , not one more secret. A passphrase on the 2-of-3 is a single point of failure in disguise. Lose it and two plates aren’t enough. The home plate’s small decoy wallet is the separate, optional place for a passphrase.

title: Recovery card
text: Time 15 min Difficulty Easy Steps 3 steps You will need Printer · Scissors The thing your heir actually grabs on the way out the door. Not the full inheritance sheet. Just the where-is-everything pointer: two plates, the wallet map, and this card. Fill in the locations by hand after the plates are stamped. This complements the inheritance sheet. It never replaces it. ⛔ No seeds. No words. Nothing on this card can spend your bitcoin. FRONT PLEBUM DOMINIUM RECOVERY 2 plates + wallet map + this card = your bitcoin. The plates are useless without the map. The map is useless without two plates. Derivation path: m/48'/0'/0'/2' (not a secret. It's how the wallet is shaped) BACK WHERE THINGS ARE Plate A: Plate B: Plate C: Wallet map: Passphrase paper: Full instructions: the inheritance sheet. This card is the map's map. A print-ready PDF at true credit-card size (3.375 × 2.125 in) is in the kit . Print it, fill in the locations by hand, keep it with the inheritance sheet. title: One key, done right
text: Time 1-2 hours Difficulty Careful Steps 8 sections You will need Your hardware wallet · Titanium plates · Pen and paper The destination of this guide is the 2-of-3 build: three keys, three places, no single point of failure. In the full build, this sheet is also the spending wallet that lives on Plate A: Seed 1 plus a passphrase, for spending money while savings sit in the vault. SEED TOUCHED THE INTERNET Coins in a phone app or on an exchange → PORT OVER · STEP 2 SEED BORN ON THE DEVICE Never typed, photographed, or stored anywhere digital → UPGRADE IN PLACE · STEP 3 The seed phrase is the wallet. The device only signs. One rule: the words go into the device itself, during recovery, and nowhere else. Never a website, never an app, never a form from an email. No hardware company will ever ask for your seed phrase. If a message asks, the message is the attack, no matter how official it looks. Step 1 · Grade your seed. Was the seed made on the device itself, or in an app? Has it ever been typed, photographed, or stored in any digital form (a notes app, a photo, a cloud drive, a password manager)? Do you hold it on paper or metal, in a place only you know? Any wrong answer: the seed counts as exposed. Step 2 is not optional. No seed yet (coins on an exchange): also Step 2. Clean seed (born on the device, never copied anywhere digital): Step 3. A device bought used, or from a marketplace seller, is not a signer. It is a suspect. Buy from the maker's own shop. Step 2 · Exposed seed: port over. 1 · VERIFY Check the files Every tool verified first ↓ 2 · BOOT OFFLINE Tails, networking disabled No Persistent Storage ↓ 3 · ROLL ONE KEY Five dice, faces 1 to 4 Two tools must agree ↓ 4 · RESTORE ON THE DEVICE Every word entered on the device itself Word 24 is a checksum. It is never invented. If the two tools disagree, stop. Write the 24 words on paper, then type them into the device on the device itself,* in its own restore menu, on its own screen. Then shut everything down. No program on a computer does the restore, not Sparrow, not Electrum, and not a text field in a companion app. If a device needs its companion app to start the restore (BitBox App for a BitBox02, Blockstream Green for a Jade), the app only opens the connection. The words still go in on the device, never typed into the computer. In the 2-of-3 build the airgapped boot signs, in Sparrow or Electrum. On this sheet the device signs. You boot your trusted online computer for Sparrow, and Sparrow meets the device afterward, in Step 6, as the watch-only wallet that builds transactions for the device to sign. The fresh seed has now lived in exactly two places: the offline boot, which forgot it, and the device. Steps 4 and 5 come before any coins move. The old device stays on as the signer, and the old seed retires. * A device adds trust in its maker: the firmware on it, the chip inside it, and the shop it came from. The trade buys something real. A key the everyday computer never holds cannot be stolen by malware on that computer, and the device screen shows every address before you sign. 1 · PAPER 24 words written down Fresh seed from the offline boot ↓ 2 · RESTORE ON THE DEVICE Typed in on its own screen Its own restore menu ↓ 3 · THE DEVICE SIGNS Boot on trusted online computer The 2-of-3 build signs in Tails ↓ 4 · SPARROW, WATCH-ONLY Builds transactions, cannot spend Step 6, after the restore ✕ WORDS NEVER GO INTO A COMPUTER Not Sparrow, not Electrum, no text field Step 3 · Clean seed: upgrade in place. Keep the seed. Nothing about it changes. The work is everything around it: passphrase (Step 4), metal (Step 5), watch-only (Step 6). Go straight to Step 4. Step 4 · Add a passphrase. WORDS ALONE Opens a different wallet, nearly empty → THE DECOY WORDS + PASSPHRASE Opens your wallet → YOUR SAVINGS A passphrase is one more secret, a word or short phrase you choose, entered on the device after the seed. On this sheet it is required. One seed in one place is why: a plate found or stolen without the passphrase opens an empty wallet. Forgotten passphrase: the coins are gone, and nobody can reset it. Handed to a scammer along with the words: it stops nothing. Words and passphrase are never kept together and never given to anyone. Write the passphrase on paper. Keep that paper in a different place from the plate. Never write it on the plate. Keep a small spending balance in the wallet without the passphrase. A plate found under pressure has something to show, and it is not your savings. Prove it works: note the first receiving address of the passphrase wallet. The restore check in Step 5 must bring back that same address. If it does not, no real money moves. Note The 2-of-3 build in this guide uses no passphrase, on purpose. Do not add one there. Three keys in three places already do the work. This sheet is one key, so the passphrase carries weight here that it never has to carry in the vault. Step 5 · Stamp it in metal. One seed, one plate, stamped the way teaches. Read the finished plate back, word by word, against the paper. Restore check: wipe the device or use a second one, restore from the plate plus the passphrase, confirm the Step 4 address comes back. Destroy the seed paper only when the restore checks out. The passphrase paper is not destroyed. It lives in its own place, apart from the plate. Step 6 · Watch-only, and the first coins. 1 · WATCH-ONLY BUILDS Sparrow, everyday computer Sees balances, cannot spend ↓ 2 · DEVICE SIGNS The seed never touches that computer ↓ 3 · WATCH-ONLY BROADCASTS The finished payment goes out Build the watch-only wallet in Sparrow from the public key the device exports. It sees balances and builds transactions. It cannot spend. Verify the first receiving address on the device screen before anything is sent to it. If the two screens disagree, stop. From an exchange: withdraw to the verified address. A small amount first if the exchange lets you split it. Confirm it lands. Then withdraw the rest. From an old software wallet: send a small test amount to the verified address. Confirm it lands. Then send the rest. When the old wallet reads zero and the move has confirmed, destroy the old seed paper. It protects nothing now, and a live-looking seed in a drawer only confuses the people who find it later. Know the limits One seed is one point of failure. A fire where the plate sleeps ends this wallet. The passphrase paper surviving somewhere else does not rebuild it. Theft of the plate plus the passphrase paper ends it. A word copied wrong and never restore-checked ends it. This sheet beats an exchange account and it beats a seed in a phone. The distance between that and the vault is real. Graduate when the stack grows, or when the amount would hurt to lose. The 2-of-3 build starts at the . The dice, the metal, the watch-only habit, and the one rule about the words all carry over. For the people after you: an heir needs the plate, the passphrase paper, and one plain note that says what they are and which device can restore them. shows how that note should read: plain words, no Bitcoin knowledge assumed, a small test send first. Stop if The device, an app, or a website asks you to type the words into a computer or a phone: stop. That is the scam, wearing the device's clothes. The two dice tools print different words: stop. Do not pick the one you like better. A restored wallet shows a different address than the one you noted: stop. No coins move. Anyone asks for your words or your passphrase, for any reason, in any message: stop. The answer is no, forever. Next. When you are ready for the vault:

title: Two devices and one dice key
text: Time 1-2 hours Difficulty Moderate Steps 8 sections You will need Two hardware devices · 5 dice · Titanium plates A 2-of-3 wallet. Two keys live on hardware devices from different makers. The third key is a dice seed that no device ever made. No one device, one maker, or one place can move the fund alone. The seed phrase is the wallet. The device only signs. One rule: the words go into the device itself, during recovery, and nowhere else. Never a website, never an app, never a form from an email. JADE device + BITBOX device + DICE rolled offline THREE KEYS. ANY TWO OPEN THE FUND. Step 1 · Buy two devices, two makers. One Jade from Blockstream’s own shop. One BitBox from BitBox’s own shop. Not two of the same box. A device bought used, or from a marketplace seller, is not a signer. Do not trust it to hold anything. Check the device before it holds anything: the maker’s own verification, the seals, the screen. A reseller device from 2026 taught this lesson with real money. Step 2 · Make the dice key. Roll it on an offline boot, the way teaches. Five dice, faces 1 to 4. Two tools must print the same 24 words. Never let a device roll its own entropy for this stack. The dice key is the key no maker touched. Write the 24 words on paper. They become a plate in Step 4. Step 3 · Build the 2-of-3 in Sparrow. Import the public keys from both devices and the dice key. Sparrow builds the wallet. It cannot spend. Verify the first receiving address on a device screen before anything is sent to it. If the screens disagree, stop. Step 4 · Back it all up in metal. Stamp the dice seed on its own plate, the way teaches. Each device seed gets its own backup, on metal or on the maker’s own backup device, kept apart from the other keys. Three keys, three places. If one place burns, the other two keys still open the fund. Step 5 · Hide the wallet map. Encrypt the descriptor the way teaches. The map alone tells a finder nothing. Store the map apart from every key. Step 6 · Practice spend, then real coins. Send a small amount in. Spend it with the two devices. Spend it once with a device and the dice key, through the offline boot, so you know that path works before it matters. Confirm each spend lands. Then move the rest. JADE device + BITBOX device → EVERYDAY SPEND ONE DEVICE either one + OFFLINE BOOT dice key → BACKUP PATH Know the limits Two devices from two makers still trust firmware. The dice key is what breaks that trust: it takes two makers failing together, plus the dice key, to move the fund. Two devices stored in one place fail together. Geography is not optional. The dice key’s offline signing is the hardest step on this sheet. Practice it on testnet first, or with a small amount, before it carries real money. For the people after you: an heir needs any two keys plus the map. The sheet walks them through it, with the dice plate standing in for one plate. Stop if A device comes from a reseller, a marketplace, or a link in a message: stop. Both devices come from the same maker: stop. One maker failing takes both keys. Anyone asks for your words, for any reason, in any message: stop. They get no answer.

title: Keystone breach exposes customer shipping addresses
text: Latest October 2026 Keystone breach exposes customer shipping addresses On October 24, 2026, Keystone disclosed a website breach that exposed customer shipping data, including home addresses tied to past hardware wallet orders. The company said private keys and funds on its devices were not affected, since that material never touches the internet. Keystone has not said how many customers were affected or how the breach happened. Why it matters here A shipping address tied to a hardware wallet order tells a thief where a holder lives, which enables physical targeting and phishing that references your real order. This guide tells you to buy devices from the maker’s own shop. Ship those orders to an address that is not your home, and treat any message about your order as suspect. Sources: AltcoinDaily

title: Two hardware failures in one year
text: October 2026 Two hardware failures in one year In July 2026, attackers drained about 1,816 bitcoin from more than 5,200 Coldcard wallets. The cause was a firmware flaw from March 2021 that left some seeds with as little as 40 bits of real randomness instead of 128. Updating the firmware did not fix seeds already made. Owners had to move their funds to new seeds. In October 2026, Ledger confirmed an unauthorized hardware implant in at least one device sold by the Southeast Asian reseller CryptoBilis. Researchers estimate $86 million to $93 million was taken from hundreds of wallets. Ledger said its own systems and direct sales were not affected, and every confirmed case so far traces to that reseller. Why it matters here Both failures break the same promise: that the device can be trusted on its own. The guide answers that three ways. Buy from the maker’s own shop, never a reseller and never a used device. Never let a device roll its own entropy: make the seed with dice on an offline boot, then import it. And for a single key, require a passphrase: researchers noted that seeds made with dice rolls or protected by a strong passphrase were not the ones drained. A device you trust less is a device you verify more. Sources: Decrypt · CoinDesk

title: Russia closes the exchange off-ramp
text: October 2026 Russia closes the exchange off-ramp Russia’s new digital-asset law (No. 282-FZ, in force since September 1) routes all crypto buying through licensed brokers and state-approved banks. The central bank’s October guidance is explicit: moving crypto from a regulated account to your own wallet is not permitted, and peer-to-peer trades between individuals end entirely on July 1, 2027. Small buyers are capped at roughly $3,800 a year: bitcoin, ether, or tether only. Nobody banned holding your own keys. They closed the door between the regulated system and self-custody. That door is the exact step this guide starts with, when you withdraw a test amount from an exchange to an address only you control. Why it matters here Rules can close an off-ramp at any time, in any country. A wallet built before you need it never has to ask permission. Build it while the door is open. Sources: Cointelegraph · TFTC

title: FTX collapses, $8 billion in customer funds missing
text: November 2022 FTX collapses, $8 billion in customer funds missing FTX was one of the largest crypto exchanges in the world, valued at $32 billion in early 2022. On November 2, 2022, CoinDesk published the balance sheet of Alameda Research, the trading firm run by the same people, and it showed billions in FTT, a token FTX had printed itself. Customers rushed to withdraw. About $6 billion left in 72 hours, and the money was not there. FTX halted withdrawals on November 8 and filed for bankruptcy on November 11, revealing a shortfall of roughly $8 billion in customer funds. Founder Sam Bankman-Fried was convicted on seven fraud and conspiracy counts in November 2023 and sentenced to 25 years in March 2024. The bankruptcy estate later repaid most customers in dollars, but priced at November 2022 values, so a customer who had held one bitcoin got back the dollar value of a bitcoin on the day the company failed, not the bitcoin. Why it matters here An exchange balance is a claim on a company, not money in your pocket. The moment withdrawals stop, that distinction becomes the whole story. This guide keeps no balance anywhere: you buy, you withdraw a test amount to an address only you control, and you verify it before the rest follows. Even a bankruptcy that pays everyone back in dollars can still take your bitcoin. Sources: Nasdaq · Wikipedia

title: Ledger breach exposes 272,000 customer addresses
text: July 2020 Ledger breach exposes 272,000 customer addresses Ledger makes hardware wallets, and in July 2020 it disclosed that an attacker had reached its e-commerce and marketing database through a third party API key. At first Ledger said about 9,500 customers had detailed records exposed, alongside more than one million email addresses. In December 2020 the full database appeared on a public forum, and the real count was about 272,000 detailed records: names, postal addresses, and phone numbers of people who had ordered a device. No keys and no funds were touched. The damage was different: years of phishing emails and texts aimed at recovery phrases, SIM swaps, and extortion threats, all aimed at people whose home addresses were now in criminal hands. Ledger later confirmed that rogue members of its e-commerce provider’s support team had also exported customer records in April and June 2020. Why it matters here Order data is physical security data. A home address tied to a hardware wallet order tells a criminal what you own and where you keep it, and that data stays dangerous for years after the breach. Order from the maker’s shop, ship to an address that is not your home, and treat any message about your order as suspect. Sources: Ledger · CoinDesk

title: QuadrigaCX dies with its founder, $190 million locked away
text: January 2019 QuadrigaCX dies with its founder, $190 million locked away QuadrigaCX was Canada’s largest crypto exchange when its founder, Gerald Cotten, died in India in December 2018 at age 30. He alone held the passwords to the company’s cold wallets. His widow had his encrypted laptop and no password, and no one else at the company could open the wallets. About 115,000 customers were owed roughly $190 million. The exchange filed for bankruptcy in April 2019. In June 2020, Ontario’s securities regulator concluded the operation had been a fraud and a Ponzi scheme, with Cotten trading against customers under aliases. Whether the keys were truly lost or never existed, the result for customers was the same: the money was gone. Why it matters here One person holding every key is the failure this guide is built to remove. A 2-of-3 spread across three keys and three places survives any single death, loss, or theft, and the inheritance sheet exists so the people you trust can still open the fund when you cannot. Sources: CoinDesk · Wikipedia

title: Mt. Gox loses 850,000 bitcoin
text: February 2014 Mt. Gox loses 850,000 bitcoin Mt. Gox was the world’s largest bitcoin exchange, handling more than 70 percent of all bitcoin transactions in early 2014. On February 24, 2014, it suspended trading and went offline. Four days later it filed for bankruptcy in Tokyo, admitting about 850,000 bitcoin had gone missing, worth roughly $450 million at the time. About 200,000 were later recovered from an old wallet. The rest were never found. Investigations later showed the exchange had been losing coins to attackers since 2011, slowly, through flaws in how it tracked withdrawals. Creditors waited a decade: repayments through Kraken and Bitstamp began in July 2024, and the deadline for the remaining distributions runs to October 31, 2026. Why it matters here This is the original lesson of the site. Coins left on an exchange are the exchange’s coins until you withdraw them, and no reputation or size changes that. The practice spend exists so you prove the withdrawal step with a small amount before your savings ever move. Sources: The Block · Wikipedia
